Reasoning summary:
- Greedy Steiner trees are highly order-sensitive; fully shuffled orders explore a much richer set of starting trees than varying only the first destination (which duplicates the per-dst seed candidates already present).
- `improve` is monotone (accepts only strict cost reductions), and the final selection takes the minimum over all improved candidates, so extra candidates and a larger improved pool can only reduce total cost without risking correctness or the success rate.
- These changes reproduce and extend the strategy that achieved the best recorded cost (627.13) while keeping the multi-source and Steiner-tree candidates that were already validated.
